seoTitle: How to Sync Asana With Google Calendar
metaDescription: Learn how to sync Asana deadlines to Google Calendar in 2026 using a live iCal feed link, so due dates stay updated automatically.
intro: Rather than manually copying deadlines between apps, Asana can generate a live calendar feed link that Google Calendar subscribes to directly. This guide covers finding that feed URL, subscribing to it in Google Calendar, and confirming updates flow through automatically as tasks change.

steps.heading: Open the Calendar tab in Asana
steps.body: Go to a project or your personal My Tasks section and switch to the Calendar view tab.

steps.heading: Find the export and sync options
steps.body: Open the project dropdown menu to locate the export and sync settings.

steps.heading: Generate and copy the iCal feed link
steps.body: Generate a secure, real-time iCal subscription link and copy the URL.

steps.heading: Subscribe in Google Calendar
steps.body: In Google Calendar, open the calendar addition panel and choose the From URL subscription option, then paste in the Asana sync link.

steps.heading: Name and verify the calendar
steps.body: Name your new integrated calendar, customize its overlay color, and confirm that due date updates in Asana reflect automatically.

faq.question: How often does the Google Calendar feed refresh?
faq.answer: iCal subscriptions typically refresh on Google's own schedule rather than instantly, so there may be a short delay before changes appear.

faq.question: Can I sync my personal My Tasks list, not just a project?
faq.answer: Yes, the same export process works from your personal My Tasks calendar view, not only from a shared project.

faq.question: Does this sync work both ways?
faq.answer: No, the iCal feed is a one-way sync from Asana into Google Calendar, so editing an event in Google Calendar won't change the Asana task.

faq.question: Can I unsubscribe from the calendar feed later?
faq.answer: Yes, you can remove the subscribed calendar from Google Calendar's settings at any time without affecting your Asana data.
